[ASSISTANT_SAID] The limitations of the Canvas API include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Limited functionality for 2D graphics and not suitable for complex animations or 3D graphics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Lack of interactivity compared to SVG, making it difficult to create interactive graphics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Difficulty with text rendering on the canvas, requiring additional JavaScript code.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Performance issues when rendering large, complex graphics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Difficulty with accessibility for visually impaired users.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Alternatives to the Canvas API for creating complex animations and 3D graphics in HTML5 include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. WebGL: A low-level API for creating 3D graphics with direct access to the graphics card.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Three.js: A lightweight 3D library for WebGL with a high-level API.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Greensock: A JavaScript animation library for creating complex animations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. SVG: A markup language for creating vector graphics, accessible by default.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. CSS Animations: Built-in CSS feature for simple animations using properties like transform and opacity.  
[USER] User plans to start with the basics of Three.js and work their way up.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for getting started with Three.js include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Start with the basics, understanding the coordinate system, cameras, and lighting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Use examples and tutorials available online to learn how to use the library.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Experiment with different materials and textures for more interesting 3D scenes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Optimize performance using techniques like culling and LOD.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Join the Three.js community for resources and connections with other developers.  
[USER] User intends to start with the Three.js Fundamentals series and then move on to other tutorials as needed.
